subject: Performance gap analysis & MAP: streaming TTFT targets and close timeline
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Lawson <eve.lawson@curacloud.com>, Sara Chen <sara.chen@orchardhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Performance gap analysis & MAP: streaming TTFT targets and close timeline

Eve / Sara —

Thanks for taking time last week. As we discussed in the workshop, the primary gating items for CuraCloud to go live are:
- streaming TTFT under 350ms p50 for typical chat prompts,
- p95 below 1.1s, p99 below 2.2s at 8 concurrent users per replica, and
- confident throughput at 160 req/s with graceful tail-latency.

Attached is a short performance gap analysis (curacloud_map_v2.pdf) and an initial benchmarking plan. High level ask for this thread: align on MAP milestones and close timeline so we can schedule a dedicated canary in the next slot. Proposed MAP milestones:

1) Perf eval kickoff (this week) — we run a controlled sweep of batch/concurrency/quantization; collect TTFT & streaming latencies.
2) Canary config proposal — runtime knobs + autoscale policy for Dedicated pool (by 2028-03-27).
3) Customer acceptance run — two-day run with production traces and traffic replay (target week of 2028-04-03).
4) SLA & contract signature — finalize after acceptance.

I’ve asked Marissa and Aditya to run the initial bench and share raw results by EOD tomorrow. Monica will own the MAP doc and timeline in Drive.

Next steps for CuraCloud: please confirm the acceptance window that works on your side and whether you have a preferred set of production prompts (we can also use the anonymized corpus you shared).

TG — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Eve Lawson <eve.lawson@curacloud.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance gap analysis & MAP: streaming TTFT targets and close timeline

Karthik / team —

Quick update on the bench sweep I ran this afternoon (attached: ttft_streaming_results.csv). Test bed: app-gen chat prototype (seq len 160), model = rw-chat-v1.3 (int8), G5-like instance type, request mix = 60% streaming, 40% non-streaming. Key findings:

- Baseline (single replica, no batching): TTFT streaming p50 = 320ms, p95 = 980ms, p99 = 1.9s; non-streaming p50 = 280ms.
- With continuous batching (batch window 12ms): p50 improved marginally (~10%), p95 improved to 850ms, p99 to 1.6s.
- Concurrency sweep: at 8 concurrent users (synthetic concurrency), observed p99 spike to 2.6s on cold KV cache; warm cache p99 ~1.9s.
- Throughput plateau: ~165 req/s sustained with autoscale set to min=1, max=8 replicas; above that we saw queueing and TTFT degradation.

I added annotations in the CSV for the runs most representative of the customer shape. I’ll follow up with the raw traces and the k8s logs (concurrency-sweep-k8s.log) for the one run where p99 spiked.

Notes / suggestion: we can tighten p95 by: 1) enabling prefix KV caching for repeated sessions, 2) reducing batch window for chat streaming to 6–8ms for tail-sensitive endpoints, and 3) pinning a higher priority lane for interactive users during canary.

-Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance gap analysis & MAP: streaming TTFT targets and close timeline

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick bench. This looks promising and close to our targets. A few clarifying Qs from our infra team:

1) For the KV cache warm/cold behavior — can you reproduce warm-cache conditions using our session traces? We rely heavily on session affinity (multi-turn dialogues).
2) The throughput plateau at 165 req/s — is that per-replica or cluster-wide? What were CPU/GPU utilisations on those runs?
3) Any functional regression risk with int8 path vs fp16 for our intents that include structured extraction?

Acceptance window — we prefer Apr 3–4 for the two-day run. We’ll provide a scrubbed prompt set by EOD Friday.

Eve
Infrastructure Lead, CuraCloud
Eve.Lawson@curacloud.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Lawson <eve.lawson@curacloud.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Mar 2028 11:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance gap analysis & MAP: streaming TTFT targets and close timeline

Eve —

Answers inline:
1) Warm vs cold KV: I replayed a 10k-session sample from CuraCloud (anonymized) — warm-cache runs (session affinity preserved) push p99 down roughly 15–20% compared to cold-cache. I’ll attach the specific run IDs to the Drive notes.

2) Throughput plateau: 165 req/s was cluster-wide for the Dedicated pool with autoscale up to 8 replicas. Per-replica sustained was ~22 req/s for streaming-heavy mix due to per-connection overhead; non-streaming sustained higher per-replica. GPU util: 62–78% on the plateau runs; CPU spiking on the ingress side during bursts. See concurrency-sweep-k8s.log for metrics.

3) int8 vs fp16 functional risk: for the extraction intents we tested, int8 produced equivalent entity spans on our eval suite (delta F1 < 0.8%). We do recommend a short regression eval during acceptance with your production prompt set — that’s part of the MAP acceptance checklist.

Operational suggestion: for the canary, start with mixed quantization (fp16 for extraction endpoints, int8 for conversational tail) and monitor quality gates; fallback to fp16 per-route if regressions are detected.

-Aditya

From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@orchardhealth.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Eve Lawson <eve.lawson@curacloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance gap analysis & MAP: streaming TTFT targets and close timeline

All —

Appreciate the clear plan and the bench notes. CuraCloud confirms Apr 3–4 as the acceptance window. Two quick asks before we start the run:

- Please provide a one-page canary playbook (runbook) that lists the exact runtime flags, autoscale thresholds, and rollback triggers (we need this for our change review).
- Include the metric hooks you’ll emit for our monitoring (token-level latency, per-route p99, cache hit rate).

If those are included in the Drive MAP doc by Monday, we can lock the signature to follow within 48 hours of a successful acceptance run.

Thanks — Sara
VP, Product Operations | Orchard Health (partnering via CuraCloud)
